transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess… I had a little trouble at work. I’m a personal care aide, and during a staff meeting I got kind of worked up about fall prevention. I started, uh, acting out a whole drill with the chairs and waving my arms around, showing how people could fall or how to stop it.

I know that probably sounds odd. I wasn’t trying to cause a scene, but I just couldn’t seem to stop, even when people were telling me to sit down. So… they thought maybe I should come in and talk to someone.
Before or during that staff meeting, did you feel unusually energetic, like your thoughts were racing, or like you didn’t need as much sleep as usual?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but sometimes I do get kind of… keyed up, I guess. Like on those days I’ll start cleaning out closets, rewriting the care checklists, thinking I can plan a whole health fair for the church, and I’ll be calling people before breakfast because it feels like it all needs to happen right then.  

I know that’s probably a bit much. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
After one of those times when you felt really keyed up and busy, did you ever feel like you crashed—like you were really down, had trouble getting motivated, or lost interest in things for a while?

Yeah… I guess there are times after that where I kind of slow way down. I don’t know if I’d call it a “crash,” exactly, but my wife says I’ll just sit in the living room with the TV on low and not really do much.

I mean, I know there are chores that need doing, simple stuff, and I used to call people from church more… but I just don’t seem to get to it. It’s not that I’m trying to be lazy or anything. I just kind of… sit there. Does that make sense?
